name: Durlax Top Surface Limited
sector: Acrylic and modified solid surfaces; polymer laminates
summary: Durlax has demonstrated rapid standalone revenue growth, but three consecutive years of negative operating cash flow make it a financing-dependent growth watchlist, not a proven cash compounder. FY2026 revenue ₹184.55 crore and PAT ₹12.64 crore contrast with ₹12.36 crore operating cash outflow; June-quarter other income supplies most PBT. At the October 19 ₹60.85 close, current equity is about ₹176.05 crore before warrant conversion. BQS 4.88; Growth Quality GQS 5.00, capped for persistent poor cash realization; IAS NS because current operating and deployment economics remain material uncertainties. Full conditional five-year models give approximately −39.4%/4.8%/33.8% annual bear/base/bull returns, not probabilities or executable targets. [S1][S10][S11][S18]
identity_note: Audited note 2 confirms June 26 2024 NSE Emerge listing; active SM master and actual rights allotment establish current shares.
score_note: Full canonical BQS and GQS audited; GQS capped at 5 for persistent cash weakness. IAS NS for material recurring earnings and capital-deployment uncertainty. REV is limited to 8 by Medium confidence; corrected BQS 4.88 and raw GQS 5.95. Ranking eligibility is unchanged, while any BQS ordering must use the corrected value.

GOV.reason: Audits, monitoring and detailed capital terms permit review; concentrated family control, repeated equity funding, related advances and monitored CC co-mingling require scrutiny. No substantiated diversion or fraud finding.

MOAT.reason: Brands, dealer access and product know-how offer differentiation, but concentrated buyers/suppliers, imported substitutes and direct domestic rivalry limit demonstrated pricing power. Narrow trade relief is not a broad moat.

REV.reason: Revenue expanded above 30% CAGR using both pre-COVID FY2020–26 and FY2023–26 windows; comparable standalone scope. No upgrade for the strong single quarter or prospective acquisition; no verified material gross/net or acquired-growth distortion. The historical-growth rubric starts at 9, but v3.0 section 3 limits a Medium-confidence historical factor to 8. Confidence remains Medium; this ceiling is not a change in revenue evidence.

DUR.reason: Import substitution, existing brand channels and 81% utilization offer practical runway, but costly new brands and sanitary expansion need funding and proven demand rather than a TAM claim.

CAP.reason: Core NOPAT against closing-capital changes suggests mixed, roughly cost-of-capital-range incremental returns; late rights receipt distorts average capital. New product/acquisition cohorts are unproven. Not enough for excess-return scoring or a persistent value-destruction override.

CASH.reason: Three successive negative CFO years despite positive profit, large supplier advances and rising debtors establish persistent weak realization, not merely one temporary capex build. Cash-quality override applies.

BAL.reason: Rights capital and warrant deposit help, but high bank usage, operating cash deficits, tax contingencies and optional future subscriptions constrain survival flexibility; no verified default.

EXEC.reason: Sales scaling and completed rights deployment demonstrate activity, but cash conversion and brand-launch returns have not matched accounting growth. New deployment requires measured outcomes.

EARN.reason: FY2026 operating profit improved, but unrealized FX, quarter other income, weakening core quarter margin and large dilution weaken per-share quality. Earnings are not scored as cash conversion again.

R.reason: Material uncertainty in recurring quarter earnings, supplier-advance recovery, actual current bank cash and unspecified sanitary/new-brand deployment economics prevents a combined point valuation and robust return/downside distribution. Conditional annual models are completed.

D.reason: Material uncertainty in recurring quarter earnings, supplier-advance recovery, actual current bank cash and unspecified sanitary/new-brand deployment economics prevents a combined point valuation and robust return/downside distribution. Conditional annual models are completed.

P.reason: Material uncertainty in recurring quarter earnings, supplier-advance recovery, actual current bank cash and unspecified sanitary/new-brand deployment economics prevents a combined point valuation and robust return/downside distribution. Conditional annual models are completed.

L.reason: Observed median 5% reference exit supports 9 before a two-point execution adjustment for 24.34% one-lot concentration, fewer-than 100-PAN alert and volatile price range. All observed dates traded; no generic-SME missing-day penalty.

gates.reason: Promoter control, substantial dilution, related advances and monitored funds co-mingling warrant safeguards; no established fraud/diversion finding.

Audited statements and restricted-cash bridge reconcile; quarter other income and latest supplier/deployment balances limit normalized earnings, not the integrity of all accounts. Small historical reconciliation differences are not a critical hold.
Cash deficits and object spending may require additional borrowing despite rights and warrant deposit; future conversion optional, high facility usage, proposed limits not committed headroom.
All observed sessions traded, but 24.34% reference-position lot, concentrated PANs, volatility and unverified live depth limit execution.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Durlax Top Surface Limited, INE0OUW01013, NSE SME DURLAX; June 26 2024 listing independently supported by audited capital note. Cutoff October 20 2026, last official trade October 19, standalone Indian AS scope. Five-year nominal shareholder model, 15% analyst return hurdle, ₹5 lakh reference position, no allocation recommendation. All four gates are Conditional: governance and funds-use controls, earnings/advance visibility, future funding and lot/depth limitations. No evidenced gate failure or blanket clean-governance assurance. Historical statements and official market data have higher confidence than current recurring earnings and planned deployment. [S1][S8][S11][S18][S19]

sections.title: Scorecard & Factor Audit
sections.text: BQS 4.88 uses GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 2, BAL 4 and EXEC 5 at canonical weights. GQS raw 5.95, final 5.00; EARN 4 and persistent CASH 2 cap growth quality at 5. IAS retains L 7 and quality contribution but R/D/P are NS; weights are not reallocated. CAP 5 is a mixed-return assessment, not an unsupported precision claim. Ordinary reported standalone growth is scoreable despite no explicit organic label, because no material acquired scope reset was identified. Sensitive assumptions and complete arithmetic remain in the factor/score audit. [S1][S2][S5][S11][S18] The Medium-confidence ceiling reduces the historical REV factor from its rubric starting score of 9 to 8; all other factors are unchanged.

sections.title: Business Model & Industry Position
sections.text: The Vapi manufacturer sells interior solid surfaces under LUXOR, ASPIRON and HERONITEZ and is launching TRUDO polymer laminates. Buyers pay for appearance, fabrication, hygiene and durability in commercial/residential interiors. The business absorbs resin/mineral inputs, inventory, dealer credit and supplier advances before collections; revenue is not a cash-light software-style stream. Rating research identifies 49% top-three buyer and 54% supplier concentration, 11% exports and 5% imports with unhedged FX exposure. Stylam is a direct acrylic/modified-surface competitor; Marbonex is another named domestic producer in DGTR records; Greenlam is an adjacent laminate/wood-surfacing and distribution benchmark, not a like-for-like acrylic multiple. No unsupported peer P/E ranking is used. [S1][S5][S12][S21][S23][S24]

sections.title: Moat & Competitive Advantage
sections.text: Brand and fabricator/dealer familiarity may create repeat orders, but no independently verified retention cohort, sustained realized-price premium or structural cost advantage establishes a strong moat. Historical import intensity creates an opportunity and competitive pressure simultaneously. DGTR’s 94% import share refers to the 2022–23 investigation period, not FY2026. A five-year anti-dumping levy was implemented in March 2025; product exclusions mean it cannot be applied to every modified surface or polymer laminate. Total issuer capacity also covers products outside the investigation, so cross-company sheet-capacity rankings are unreliable. GOV and MOAT are therefore separate: compliance certificates do not prove competitive advantage. [S1][S21][S22][S23]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Earnings Quality
sections.text: Revenue grew from ₹30.49 crore in FY2020 to ₹184.55 crore in FY2026; the pandemic FY2021 trough ₹19.55 crore is shown but not used alone to sell the CAGR. FY2023–26 grew from ₹66.74 crore, likewise above 30% annually. FY2026 normalized EBITDA ₹22.49 crore excludes ₹2.32 crore other income, including ₹2.108 crore unrealized FX, and adds back ₹0.2626 crore prior gratuity. June-quarter revenue ₹55.99 crore versus ₹29.59 crore was strong, but core EBITDA only ₹2.7194 crore or 4.86%; ₹3.3443 crore other income versus ₹3.7193 crore PBT prevents extrapolating profit. The rating’s ₹58.93 crore quarter sales is not substituted for the primary table. Reported FY2026 EPS ₹7.22 is weighted-average; PAT divided by current shares is about ₹4.37, before warrant dilution. No single-quarter trajectory score upgrade. [S1][S4][S5][S10][S11][S12]

sections.title: Runway, Reinvestment & Capital Allocation
sections.text: Management reports 81% utilization, providing some immediate headroom but also future expansion needs. Rights proceeds ₹49.218 crore funded plant/shed, working capital and TRUDO launch, while warrants propose ₹14.5 crore sanitary acquisition,₹16.5 crore DLZINC launch,₹14.5 crore expansion and ₹3.5 crore general purposes. These are distinct reinvestment cohorts; no target purchase economics are disclosed sufficiently to invent acquired profits. A financing-side invested-capital proxy retaining restricted deposits gives roughly ₹102.90 crore FY2025 and ₹141.93 crore FY2026, after subtracting free cash and bank cooperative investments. Normalized NOPAT increases from about ₹8.66 crore to ₹15.02 crore, an approximately 16.3% one-year incremental proxy, near a 12–16% analyst cost-of-capital range rather than decisively above it; late March rights cash and annual averages limit inference. Closing-capital returns do not prove new-brand unit economics. [S1][S2][S6][S8][S9]

sections.title: Governance & Minority Shareholder Protection
sections.text: March promoter group held 51.45%, led by Shravan and Lalit Suthar; related warrants could alter control on conversion. IPO gross ₹40.8 crore included ₹12.24 crore OFS, so only ₹28.56 crore fresh issue funded the company. Rights and warrants add major dilution after the IPO. Auditors gave an unmodified opinion; secretarial compliance reported no exceptions within its scope, neither a guarantee of conduct nor proof of cash recoverability. Related sales/purchases, director loan turnover, remuneration ₹0.42 crore each and Suthario advance ₹0.8005 crore merit commercial-terms review. CARO’s ₹0.1675 crore overdue demand advances are small relative to profit and not alone a critical integrity hold. Monitoring records transfers into a CC account and co-mingling of rights funds; this weakens tracing but is not a finding of diversion. April CFO appointment and September AGM were checked. [S1][S5][S8][S9][S13][S14][S15][S16] June 30 shareholding confirms 14, 884, 661 promoter shares (51.45%) and 9, 190, 000 promoter warrants; full conversion would imply 61.34% promoter ownership. Its declaration reports no promoter pledge, non-disposal undertaking or other encumbrance at June 30, not a guarantee through October. Lock-in is a transfer restriction, not a pledge. [S26]

sections.title: Financial Forensics & Cash Conversion
sections.text: FY2024–26 CFO totals−₹35.75 crore against approximately ₹25.18 crore prospectus-restated/current PAT, a negative 142% conversion ratio. Using original FY2024 PAT does not change the conclusion. Capex is separately classified and does not explain negative CFO. FY2026 receivables rose ₹28.93 crore and supplier advances reached ₹17.00 crore from ₹0.64 crore; inventory fell ₹7.68 crore but did not release enough cash. Receivables older than a year ₹0.8817 crore were unprovided; balances are not presumed unrecoverable. Cash-flow close ₹14.5156 crore reconciles to cash/bank ₹15.9450 crore less ₹1.4294 crore LC-margin FD; ₹3.0826 crore noncurrent deposits are also not free opening cash. Restated FY2022–24 profit bridges adjust depreciation, deferred taxes and prior-period charges; restatement itself is not adverse. FY2024 prospectus audited-profit starting value ₹3.9364 crore differs modestly from later annual comparative ₹3.9934 crore, a ₹0.057 crore unresolved difference, not a critical financial-reliability failure. FY2026 gratuity correction is explicit. Current contingent tax ₹29.4586 crore less already-paid deposits ₹0.9687 crore enters severe cash stress, not an asserted liability judgment. [S1][S2][S3][S5]

sections.title: Valuation & Scenario Returns
sections.text: The full attached model starts with actual March cash ₹14.5156 crore, debt ₹40.4012 crore and operating WC ₹112.3024 crore, not a forecast ratio imposed backward. Current shares 28.932198 million and optional 10.315790 million warrants are matched to deposit/balance cash. Rights cash is already in opening balances; remaining rights capex ₹4.0499 crore, launch ₹5.18 crore and issue cost ₹0.26 crore are charged once. Proposed warrant acquisition, launch and expansion are separately phased with subscription cash. Unknown acquired profit is not fabricated; acquisition capital has explicit terminal recovery. Base 15% sales growth, 8.5% first-year/12% subsequent core EBITDA margin, 60% WC/sales, 11.5% funding cost and 8× terminal EBITDA yield ₹77.03 or 4.8% annual return; peak debt about ₹70.84 crore requires uncommitted additional borrowing. Bear yields ₹5.03 and bull ₹260.95. Average-debt interest circularity, taxes, maintenance/expansion capex, dilution, restricted-deposit recovery, no-conversion/no-deployment sensitivities and severe tax/impairment cases are explicit. These are illustrative stresses, not bounds. No probability-weighted point value or numeric IAS is defensible until recurring earnings, collections and actual deployment economics improve in evidence. [S1][S6][S8][S9][S10][S11][S18] Opening-claim review, 20 October 2026: the model now offsets ₹0.0837 crore separately reported TDS reimbursement against opening tax in FY2027, conditionally reducing that payment from ₹4.6621 crore to ₹4.5784 crore, and includes conditional terminal recovery of ₹0.0995 crore accrued deposit interest. A no-recovery case is supplied. These assets were excluded from operating working capital, so recovery is not counted twice. Employee, statutory and other payables and both gratuity portions were already included in net working capital. Appeal deposits remain netted only against the severe disputed-tax cash claim. Deployment, recurring earnings and financing gaps still prevent a supported IAS.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Map
sections.text: Loss pathways are specific: supplier advances or dealer receivables do not convert, quarter core margin weakness persists, raw-material/customer concentration prevents price recovery, brand launches consume funds without profitable repeat sales, optional warrants lapse while plans continue, and tax appeals create cash demand. High bank usage leaves little verified flexibility; proposed rated facilities are not sanctioned spare cash. Severe modeled 15% opening-WC impairment is noncash, then replacement funding is charged once; tax stress pays only the amount above existing deposits. This can eliminate equity without alleging present insolvency. Conversely, advance recovery, profitable expansion and better WC can release substantial cash, explaining the wide bull case. No claimed court outcome or probability is invented. [S1][S8][S11][S12]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: A five-year 5× price is ₹304.25 and 10× is ₹608.50, requiring 38.0% and 58.5% annual price growth. At full modeled warrant dilution and the base terminal net-debt bridge, 8× EBITDA requires roughly ₹156.0/₹305.3 crore EBITDA, or ₹1300/₹2544 crore revenue at 12% margin. These algebraic hurdles are not demand forecasts. Bull reaches about 4.29×, still below 5×. Sustained high growth alone is insufficient without funded collections and per-share earnings after dilution. Classification: speculative and not demonstrated. [S1][S9][S10][S18]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: At each new result, reconcile operating collections and supplier advances against March ₹16.9972 crore, debtors ₹63.9682 crore and three-year negative CFO. Obtain the next balance sheet and bank availability rather than extrapolating the rating. Explain June ₹3.3443 crore other income and core margin recovery; verify launch accounting/prepayments to avoid counting cash twice. Track each warrant conversion, receipt, allotment and earmarked deployment through December 2027, with signed acquisition price/ownership/target accounts before adding profits. Reconcile rights monitoring CC transfers and vendor evidence, review Suthario commercial terms, promoter encumbrances and current shareholding, and obtain updated tax appeal status. Thesis breaks include sustained negative CFO despite flat sales, material uncollectible advances, unfunded commitments or unexplained related diversion; ordinary small reconciliations are not automatic gate failures. Check live bid/ask depth and lot feasibility before any transaction. [S1][S8][S10][S11][S12][S20]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Financing-dependent, high-growth surface-materials watchlist with weak demonstrated cash quality; not an evidence-backed compounder or price-only bargain. BQS is 4.88, a middle-range quality assessment and GQS capped despite strong REV. Base return is below the 15% analyst hurdle; substantial upside requires collections, margins and execution beyond the present proof. IAS remains NS for concrete material operating/deployment uncertainty, not because probabilities were simply left uncalibrated. All gates remain Conditional rather than failed. No buy/sell or portfolio-size instruction is implied. [S1][S8][S11][S18]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary review covers original FY2020–21 history, prospectus FY2022–24 restatements, original FY2024 and annual FY2025–26 accounts, rights offer/addendum, EGM/warrant terms, monitoring, June-quarter results and September rating. April–October exchange refresh includes CFO appointment, financing, AGM and depository compliance; issuer archive checked separately. Official daily market/security/decoded surveillance data are used, not the undated CSV snapshot. Direct and adjacent peers are qualitatively distinguished. Remaining gaps are current advance recoverability, quarter other-income composition, June balance-sheet/deployment mapping, acquisition terms/unit economics and live executable depth. No complete Gazette legal-status certification, current market-share estimate or third-party solvency guarantee is claimed. Full annual scenarios and sensitivities are supplied despite these gaps. valuation.status: Complete conditional annual operating, funding and terminal-equity model; not a point valuation
valuation.units: INR crore, shares as number, per-share INR
valuation.opening_WC_formula: 42.2571 inventory + 63.9682 receivables + 20.0421 other current assets - 0.0995 interest - 0.0837 TDS - 0.9687 appeal deposits + 0.2734 security deposits - 9.1786 payables - 3.5251 other liabilities - 0.0849 current gratuity - 0.2979 long gratuity = 112.3024
methodology: March 2026 actual reconciled balances anchor the model. No forecast WC ratio is applied backward. A disclosed Suthario advance remains within opening assets because its exact mapping is unresolved; it is not deducted twice.

Rights proceeds were received before opening and are not added again. Remaining verified post-March rights uses enter FY2027 once: capex 4.0499, launch expense/cash 5.18 and issue cost 0.26. Minor rounding differences are not modeled as missing cash.

Baseline maintenance capex excludes the separate rights-funded building and warrant expansion. No historical PPE purchase is charged again. Depreciation follows opening PPE plus half current capex at an explicit assumption, not a verified asset-life schedule.

June warrant deposit is known cash, not current equity shares. Optional remaining subscription enters FY2028 together with conversion shares, within December 2027 deadline. Zero conversion preserves all actual rights shares and assumes forfeiture of the deposit under the terms.

Each receipt phase funds proportional planned acquisition 14.5, launch 16.5 and expansion 14.5 out of total 49.0. The remaining 3.5 GCP supports ordinary cash needs already in operating costs and is not charged twice. Deployment fractions are illustrative choices, not verified contractual obligations.

No unidentified acquired revenue, profits or goodwill are fabricated. Acquisition expenditure earns no incremental profits here and has explicit terminal recovery sensitivity. Expansion may support assumed core revenue growth but has no second terminal asset addition.

Known rights launch and proposed warrant launch are expensed and paid once. Actual prepaid inventory/marketing capitalization could alter timing; no quarterly balance sheet resolves it. Forecast operating WC explicitly excludes these modeled new launch prepayments.
Positive taxable profit is taxed at 25 percent; tax benefit from impairments or disputed tax payment is conservatively not assumed. Existing tax payable is paid once separately from current tax.

Interest solves average opening/closing debt circularly, including half-year new draws. A one-crore operating cash floor is assumed. Additional debt is a funding requirement, not an available committed facility; proposed rating limits are not headroom.

Noncash WC impairment reduces usable opening assets and is added back to CFO while replacement investment is funded once. Severe tax cash stress subtracts appeal deposits already paid, avoiding double payment.

Opening-claim audit 20 October 2026: TDS reimbursement 0.0837 crore, excluded from operating WC, is assumed available against the 4.6621 crore opening tax liability in FY2027, giving net payment 4.5784 crore. This timing is conditional, with a no-recovery sensitivity. Accrued interest 0.0995 crore, also excluded from WC, has conditional terminal recovery at the deposit recovery fraction, without extrapolated interest income. Statutory, employee, other payables and both gratuity portions are already included once in net WC. Appeal deposits are excluded and netted only against the severe disputed-tax claim, not recovered again.

Restricted bank deposits are not opening spendable cash. Terminal release/recovery is separately conditional; appellate deposits are not credited again. No dividends or future equity rescue is assumed.

These scenarios and stresses are analyst assumptions, not verified upper/lower bounds. They do not resolve latest cash, supplier-advance recoverability, other-income persistence, proposed acquisition terms or deployment returns. IAS remains NS for those material inputs, not simply unknown scenario probabilities.

Changes to modeled net WC already fund the net replacement/settlement requirement; no second full opening-benefit payment or terminal deduction is made.
